number.why: The abstract explicitly reports dulaglutide versus placebo HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79–0.99 for the first 3-point MACE event in the intention-to-treat population over trial follow-up. The registry gives identical numerical bounds but labels the CI 95.33%; confirmation is therefore specific to the stated abstract provenance.

quotes.span: The primary outcome was the first occurrence of the composite endpoint of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (including unknown causes), which was assessed in the intention-to-treat population.

During a median follow-up of 5·4 years (IQR 5·1-5·9), the primary composite outcome occurred in 594 (12·0%) participants at an incidence rate of 2·4 per 100 person-years in the dulaglutide group and in 663 (13·4%) participants at an incidence rate of 2·7 per 100 person-years in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·88, 95% CI 0·79-0·99; p=0·026).

entry.why: The packet establishes adults with type 2 diabetes randomized to a GLP-1 receptor agonist or placebo in a double-blind trial with the required endpoint. Restriction to older adults with cardiovascular disease or risk factors does not violate the question's eligibility.

quotes.span: We assessed the effect of the GLP-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide on major adverse cardiovascular events when added to the existing antihyperglycaemic regimens of individuals with type 2 diabetes with and without previous cardiovascular disease and a wide range of glycaemic control.
This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was done at 371 sites in 24 countries.

Men and women aged at least 50 years with type 2 diabetes who had either a previous cardiovascular event or cardiovascular risk factors were randomly assigned (1:1) to either weekly subcutaneous injection of dulaglutide (1·5 mg) or placebo.

missed: The ruling omitted the abstract–registry CI-level discrepancy (95% versus 95.33%), quoted above. This does not overturn the abstract-sourced numerical match, but the two confidence levels should not be treated as interchangeable. The stored statistical-model label 'rate / person-time' also needs correction: the registry states, 'The primary analysis model was a Cox proportional hazards regression model for the time to the first occurrence of a primary endpoint event, with treatment as a fixed effect using the intent-to-treat population.' (ref: evidence/held/registry/NCT01394952.json). Neither issue changes entry eligibility.
